items.title: Fact
items.body: Something that happened: a click, a screen change, speech, a grant, a revocation. Never edited, never branched.

items.title: Intent
items.body: Something someone decided, set, planned, proposed or noted. Branchable and mergeable.

items.title: Ledger
items.body: All facts. Each author keeps its own hash chain; a store accepts a fact only as the next link.

items.title: Realm
items.body: *Real* facts happened once, for everyone. *Rehearsal* facts were simulated on one branch and are only visible there.

items.title: Tree
items.body: All intents and the branches they sit on, drawn as a graph.

items.title: Branch
items.body: A line of intents. Starts from a fork point (any intent) on its parent. main is the root branch.

items.title: Head
items.body: The latest intent(s) of a branch. Two heads = two lanes wrote at once; normal, not an error.

items.title: Horizon
items.body: The moment a branch's view of reality is pinned to. Real facts after it are hidden on that branch, except those recorded in its own lanes. None = live.

items.title: Lane
items.body:
A live working session running on a branch. Several lanes can run in parallel on one or many branches.

Revision: Every ActionMap recording or conversation *session* runs in a lane. "Session" stays only as ActionMap's label for a recording run.

items.title: View
items.body: The state of a branch, or of any single point, rebuilt from its intents plus the facts visible to it.

items.title: Resume
items.body: Start a new branch at a past point, with its own lane, and carry on from there.

items.title: Merge
items.body: Bring one branch's intents into another. Recorded as an intent, with every answer you gave.

items.title: Key type
items.body: The first segment of a setting's key (mode/…, handoff/…, privacy/…, note/…). It decides the merge rule.

items.title: Merge rule
items.body: Per key type: *auto* (merges by itself, latest wins) or *ask* (you settle it). Stored as a setting, policy/merge/<type>, so it is versioned per branch.

items.title: Conflict
items.body: Both sides changed the same *ask* setting differently since they split.

items.title: Identity
items.body: A person or organisation: a signing key with a genesis fact. Needs no blockchain.

items.title: Sub-identity
items.body: A key acting for an identity with limited powers (e.g. ext:chatgpt, a venture, a role).

items.title: Device
items.body: A machine or browser with its own key (laptop, Oracle VM, phone).

items.title: Grant
items.body: A fact by which a key gives another key some capabilities. You can't grant what you don't hold.

items.title: Capability
items.body: fact.write, intent.write, branch, merge, grant, or *.

items.title: Revoke
items.body: A fact ending a grant from that moment on.

items.title: Flow
items.body:
Who must approve what, for which devices and sub-identities. Kept as intents (flow/…), so it can be branched and merged.

Revision: An approval route: which identities must approve which action, in what order. A charter is made of flows.

items.title: Actor
items.body: Anyone or anything that produces events: human, agent, outside AI, screen, system.

items.title: Mode
items.body:
observe / suggest / act, per actor and per handed-off step.

Revision: Shorthand for a grant on steps: observe / suggest / act = which step capabilities an actor holds, in which scope, until when.

items.title: Node
items.body: Any running instance: a laptop app, a VM service, a browser tab.

items.title: Hub
items.body: A node that stores and serves the log for others.

items.title: Origin
items.body: The node or key that first wrote an event.

items.title: Surface
items.body: A screen or virtual screen where actions happen.

items.title: Sync
items.body: Swap missing events in any order; every one is re-checked on arrival.

items.title: Anchor
items.body: Publishing one fingerprint of the log somewhere public, with no data. Optional, later.

items.title: Shared ledger
items.body: The ledger replicated across several identities' hubs, signed by each, with no fees (D-029).

items.title: Scope
items.body: Who a fact or intent is visible to and synced with: me, a device set, a group, public. Each scope has its own encryption key, handed out by grants.

items.title: Charter
items.body: The rules about changing rules: who may change grants, merge rules, scopes, membership, and with what approval (one owner, or a group threshold). Kept as charter/… intents.

items.title: Group / Community
items.body: An identity whose members act together under a charter.

items.title: Recovery
items.body: How an identity gets back control after losing keys (other devices, trusted people, backup phrase).

items.title: Author chain
items.body: One key's own hash chain of facts. ActionMap's "origin" (a hub) becomes this when the Rust hub lands.

items.title: Peer
items.body: Any running copy of the core. A peer holds one or more device keys.

items.title: Adapter
items.body: Native code at the edges a browser can't do: desktop capture, acting on screen, mic/speaker.

items.title: Bystander
items.body: A person who appears in recorded facts but isn't a user (a client's staff, someone on a call). Has consent rights, holds no keys.

items.title: Conformance suite
items.body: Language-neutral test cases (events in, expected views out) that the Python v0.2 and the Rust port must both pass.

items.title: Chain link
items.body: A signed statement tying an identity key to a blockchain wallet. Lets identities work with chains without depending on any one.

items.title: Clanstack
items.body: The whole ecosystem you reach from any device (D-038). Placeholder; naming/IP pass later.

items.title: Core
items.body: Clanstack's technical base (was "foundation"). Placeholder name.

items.title: App
items.body: Something built on the core. ActionMap is the first.

items.title: Pool
items.body: All compute, storage and network your authorised peers and providers offer, used as one.

items.title: Provider
items.body: An outside platform that adds capacity (Oracle, Groq, Gemini, GitHub…), on its own free or paid tier.

items.title: Placement rule
items.body: Where a piece of data or work may run, set by its scope (e.g. private → own devices only).

items.title: Cascade
items.body: The order that decides which setting wins when device, account, sub-account and group settings disagree.

items.title: Lock
items.body: A charter mark that stops a lower level overriding a setting.

items.title: Template
items.body: A reusable bundle of charter, flows, scopes, maps and layout. Re-templating = branching it, previewing, then merging.

items.title: Continuity
items.body: Carrying on the same work on another device (the Apple sense of "Handoff").

items.title: Delegation
items.body: Proposed new name for ActionMap's "hand-off" (giving a step to an agent), to avoid clashing with continuity.

items.title: Assurance level
items.body: How much proof an action needs: silent, quarantine, witness, two-device confirm.

items.title: Trust signal
items.body: What sets the assurance level: known device, usual network, sensitivity of the action, anything unusual.

items.title: Escalation
items.body: Raising the assurance level for one action; always logged with its reason.

items.title: Replication minimum
items.body: The fewest peers that must hold a piece of data, so no single device or provider can lose it.

items.title: Keys and limits
items.body:
My identity grants my laptop, my VM and ChatGPT different powers. A device can't merge unless granted; ChatGPT can't record facts; nobody can grant more than they hold; a revoked key can't write.

tested

items.title: Offline device

The VM keeps working while the laptop is offline. On reconnect they swap events in any order and end up identical; both still verify.

items.title: Rehearse before acting

An agent runs a workflow as simulated facts on a rehearsal branch; main never sees them.

items.title: Any browser

The core runs as WebAssembly in a page, with no server.

items.title: Prove it

Export a session with a proof that it hasn't changed since a given time (optional public anchor).

items.title: Devices and flows on the map
items.body:
Under each identity I add devices and sub-identities, set their keys, capabilities and approval flows from the map, and revoke them there.

partly (grants/revoke in the Lab); flows planned

items.title: Multi-person (D)
items.body:
Several identities share a ledger; each signs their own facts; consent and speaker identity decide what's shared.

planned

items.title: Lose a device, keep my identity
items.body:
My laptop is stolen. From my VM or phone I revoke its key; anything it signs after its last accepted event is refused everywhere; I recover with other devices or a backup phrase.

Owner · proposed (Q32, Q33)

items.title: Rules about rules
items.body:
Changing a merge rule, a flow or a grant on main needs the approval the charter requires; for a group, a threshold of members.

Owner, groups · proposed (Q34)

items.title: Scoped sharing
items.body:
A co-founder joins my NXK group. They sync and decrypt only the group's scope; my private scope never reaches their devices.

Collaborators · proposed (Q35)

items.title: Leave cleanly
items.body:
A member leaves. Their grants end, new group facts are encrypted with a key they don't have, and what they already had stays theirs.

items.title: Consented audit
items.body:
A client's staff are recorded only after each consents, in a scope the client owns; a bystander can ask what was recorded about them.

Clients, bystanders · proposed

items.body:
genjob, NXK or Clanstack use the same identities, ledger, tree and charters as a library, without ActionMap.

items.body:

items.title: Clanstack Studio v0
items.body: This canvas: every decision, term, story, question and asset, answered and extended here, versioned with branches.

items.title: Layer names (was 2.1 / 4.2)
items.body:
Default in force until you challenge it:
• Clanstack = the whole ecosystem (what you open on any device).
• Core = the shared base under everything (placeholder name).
• Apps = things built on the core: ActionMap, Studio, later genjob/NXK modules.

Case study: a community builds a booking app. It runs on Core, appears inside Clanstack, and its licence is its own charter setting (D-046). If 'Clanstack' also meant the core, you couldn't licence or price the core separately from what communities build.

Answer: A keep default · B one name for everything · or write your own.

items.title: Delegation vs continuity (was 4.6)
items.body:
Default: 'delegation' = giving a step to an agent; 'continuity' = carrying on your work on another device.

Case study: you say 'hand this off' on your phone. Did you mean 'let the agent do it' or 'continue this on my laptop'? Two words remove the guess, for you and for every AI reading the log.

Answer: A keep default · B one word, decided by context.

items.title: How often may security interrupt you? (was 4.7)
items.body:
Default: aim for about one extra confirmation a week on normal days; everything else is quiet, using quarantine and logs instead.

Case study 1 (quiet): Tuesday, laptop at home, you approve a delegation → no prompt.
Case study 2 (escalate): a new phone on café Wi-Fi tries to loosen a privacy rule → asks you on a second device and says why.
Case study 3 (after the fact): a write from a device that went offline 3 days ago arrives → lands in quarantine with a note, no prompt.

Answer: A ~1/week · B more careful (daily) · C quieter (<1/month).

items.title: Which settings belong to the group, which to you? (was 5.2)
items.body:
Default split, with examples:
• Group decides (locked): who can join, shared scopes, how group merges work, licence of the group's apps.
• You decide (rights floor, a group can never override): your private scope, accessibility (text size, voice), leaving and exporting your data, your own devices and keys.
• Most specific wins for everything else: layout, notifications, default views.

Answer: A keep default · B move items between lists (say which).

items.title: Objection: encrypted data can be stored anywhere, but not processed blind
items.body:
Your 4.4 default (anywhere if encrypted) works for storing and syncing: a provider holds bytes it can't read. But to transcribe, search or run an AI model on data, the machine doing it must see it decrypted.

Proposed rule: storage and sync go anywhere encrypted; processing follows placement (private → your own devices or a provider whose guarantees you accept).

Answer: A accept · B allow trusted providers to process private data too (name them).

items.title: Pooling friends' free tiers safely
items.body:
Proposed: a friend joins as their own identity and contributes their provider account under their keys (a 'contribution'). They see what runs on it, can stop it any time, and never hand over passwords. Sharing passwords or API keys usually breaks the provider's terms and puts their account at risk.

Answer: A accept · B also allow shared keys between close friends (higher ban risk).

items.title: Absorbing your other chats
items.body:
I can only see this conversation and your saved memory. To absorb everything from other chats: paste chat links or exports into Studio → Capture, one per item, and I'll break each into decisions, terms, stories and assets keyed to its source.

Answer: A I'll paste links as I go · B search my past Claude chats for Clanstack topics and propose intake items for me to approve.

items.title: First distribution/monetisation flow to test
items.body:
Options to pressure-test first:
A templates marketplace (communities sell or share canvases)
B developer access tiers (D-046)
C paid hosting/pool capacity for people without their own devices
D consulting through NXK using Studio as the delivery tool

Payments and trading carry regulation (consumer law, and crypto rules if tokens are involved); that gets checked before anything goes live.

items.title: What Studio should do next
items.body:
Studio v0 holds the record and takes answers, sketches and ideas. Next candidates:
A connect Studio to the Rust core so its versions are signed and synced like everything else
B let AIs (Claude, ChatGPT) read and write Studio directly
C phone capture improvements (quick idea → delegate → schedule)
D the Rust hub (D-037) first, then A.
